# Retention and deletion inventory

How long each category of data is kept and how it is removed today. Not a retention commitment.

| Data | Retention rule | Deletion path | Automatic |
|---|---|---|---|
| Operator credential | Held by the deployment for as long as it is configured. | Rotate or remove the environment variable. | No |
| Operator session cookie | 24 hours by default (FINCO_SESSION_HOURS), enforced on the server. | Sign out clears the cookie. The token cannot be revoked on the server before it expires. | Yes |
| Anonymous demo cookie | 24 hours by default (FINCO_DEMO_TTL_HOURS). | Expires; clearing the browser cookie ends the session. | Yes |
| Projects and cost lines | Disposable demo sessions: removed atomically after the demo TTL when inactive, including run-history activity, or by an explicitly authorized operator reset. Other data: kept until an operator removes it. | No product route deletes a project. Archiving is a soft flag. Deletion is an operator database procedure. | No |
| Scenarios and workspace state | As for projects. | As for projects (scenarios can be archived, not deleted). | No |
| Run records and exports | As for projects. | A delete function exists in the repository but nothing in the product calls it. | No |
| Run history (immutable) | Append-only while a session exists. Permanent, admin, reference and protected history is never deleted by demo clean-up. Only complete terminal disposal of an inactive expired demo session or an explicitly authorized operator demo reset removes its history. | No individual history deletion in the product. Verified demo-owned history and its projects are removed in one transaction with foreign keys enabled and full rollback on failure. Fresh history prevents TTL expiry. | No |
| Run idempotency intents (D-029) | Not automatically deleted: a database trigger refuses DELETE. Retention is an open owner decision; until it is approved rows are kept so a committed intent can always be reconciled to its exact history row. | No deletion path exists. Rows are small and are removed only by an approved, explicitly authorized retention procedure. | No |
| Save All request ledger (WS-2) | Not automatically deleted: rows are small and let an interrupted Save All be repeated safely (the same request id with an identical body returns the stored outcome; a different body under the same id is refused). Retention is an open owner decision; until it is approved rows are kept. | No deletion path exists. Rows carry identifiers and digests only and are removed only by an approved, explicitly authorized retention procedure. | No |
| Project lifecycle receipts (WF03) | Not automatically deleted. No TTL or cascading project deletion. Minimal identifier/digest receipts remain after authorized terminal demo disposal; an additional explicitly authorized retention procedure is required for erasure. | No individual receipt deletion API. Database triggers refuse UPDATE and DELETE. No automatic erasure or erasure SLA is claimed. | No |
| Non-runnable setup drafts (WF03) | Not automatically deleted. No TTL or erasure SLA. Setup drafts and their request evidence are retained until an explicitly authorized retention/disposal mechanism exists. | No product deletion path or cascading project deletion. No canonical project exists before approved promotion. | No |
| Database backups | Automatic backups: the newest 10 are kept. Manual and pre-restore safety backups are kept until removed. | Delete the backup files. Data removed from the live database remains in older backups. | Yes |
| Application and access logs | Decided by the host. An example logrotate file keeps 7 to 14 days. | Host log management. | No |
| Rate-limit counters | Cleared on restart; demo counters are purged when stale. | Restart the process. | Yes |
| Imported model files | Not retained. | Not applicable. | Yes |
